name: New South Wales
note: In New South Wales the doctor's Medical Certificate Cause of Death (or a coroner's disposal order) and the funeral director's Death Registration Statement, lodged online through eRegistry within 7 days of burial or cremation, are matched by the Registry to register the death. From the Register, death data goes to the ABS and AIHW, NSW Health's record-linkage centre, the Queensland coordinating registry for national fact-of-death data, and monthly to the AEC. Certificates are restricted to close relatives, executors and the funeral director for 30 years. The statute text could not be read (the NSW legislation host and AustLII both refused this client), so the legal duties rest on the Registry's official guidance.

steps.title: Reportable death reported to police / coroner
steps.who: Persons aware of a reportable death (violent or unnatural, sudden with unknown cause, in custody or care, etc.).
steps.trigger: A reportable death under the Coroners Act 2009.
steps.summary: Reportable deaths must be reported to police or a coroner and a doctor may not certify the cause; the coroner then issues a disposal order. The NSW legislation host refused this client, so the sections were not read.

steps.title: Doctor completes the Medical Certificate Cause of Death
steps.who: The doctor who attended the deceased or examined the body.
steps.summary: The BDMR Act 1995 requires the doctor to give the Registrar a certificate of cause of death within 48 hours. The statute text could not be read; the Registry's guidance confirms the MCCD (or a coroner's disposal order) is one of the two documents a registration needs.

steps.title: Coroner's disposal order replaces the MCCD in coronial cases
steps.trigger: A death reported to the coroner.
steps.summary: Where the coroner has jurisdiction, the Coroner's disposal order (CDO) is the document the funeral director submits with the death registration in place of the MCCD.

steps.title: Funeral director registers the death online through eRegistry
steps.who: The funeral director (or, where there is none, the person responsible for arranging the burial or cremation).

deadline.text: within 7 days of burial or cremation

steps.summary: The funeral director submits the Death Registration Statement in eRegistry; the Registry matches it with the MCCD or coroner's disposal order to complete registration. Interstate funeral directors and families without one use paper/email forms.

steps.title: Death certificate issued to close relatives, executor or funeral director
steps.who: Spouse or de facto partner, parent or child named on the certificate; the executor or the estate's solicitor; the funeral director within 30 days of registration; others with authority or an interest in the estate.
steps.trigger: Application with proof of identity (often ordered by the funeral director at registration).
steps.summary: Death certificates are restricted for 30 years; after that the record is unrestricted and searchable for family history.

steps.title: Registry supplies death data to the ABS and AIHW
steps.who: NSW Registry of Births, Deaths & Marriages.
steps.summary: Registered deaths flow to the Australian Bureau of Statistics and the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare for statistics and research.

steps.title: Registry supplies death data to the Centre for Health Record Linkage
steps.who: NSW Registry, to the NSW Centre for Health Record Linkage (NSW Health).
steps.summary: Personal and health information on deaths is linked by CHeReL for de-identified research and policy.

steps.title: Registry sends death data to the Queensland coordinating registry
steps.who: NSW Registry, to the Queensland Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages.
steps.summary: NSW deaths enter the national fact-of-death data and the Australian Death Check through the Queensland coordinating registry (see the au-commonwealth layer).

steps.title: Government agencies check their records against the Register
steps.who: NSW Police, Department of Communities and Justice, other NSW, State, Territory and Commonwealth agencies under agreement.
steps.summary: Authorised agencies confirm information they already hold against the Registry's databases; government agencies are a recognised access pathway to restricted records.

steps.title: Registry sends monthly death lists to the AEC
steps.who: The NSW Registrar as Registrar-General under the Commonwealth Electoral Act.
steps.trigger: Registration of a death of a person aged 16 or over.

deadline.text: after the beginning of each month

steps.summary: Commonwealth law; see the au-commonwealth layer.

steps.title: Authorised non-government organisations check records against the Register
steps.who: Some non-government organisations under agreement with the Registry.
steps.summary: The Registry confirms (but does not disclose new) information held by authorised third parties, including some non-government organisations.

steps.title: Australian Death Notification Service, managed by the NSW Registry
steps.who: A family member or executor; the Registry notifies the organisations nominated.
steps.summary: The NSW Registry manages the national tell-once service for private organisations (see the au-commonwealth layer).

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Registration is due within 7 days of burial or cremation, not of death; the doctor's certificate is due within 48 hours of death (statute unread).

informantDuty.note: The funeral director registers; without one, the person arranging burial or cremation does.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent medical examiner; the Registry matches the doctor's MCCD with the registration statement and reportable deaths go to the coroner.

electronicRegistration.note: Funeral directors register online through eRegistry; interstate funeral directors and families use emailed/paper forms, and the MCCD or CDO is emailed.

certificateAccess.note: Spouse/partner, parent or child named on the record, executor or estate solicitor, and the funeral director within 30 days; open after 30 years.
